strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy.linalg.pinvh on the near-singular Hermitian matrix [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]] using the project's new test_zero_eigenvalue; on the buggy revision (pinvh using the default evr eigh driver) the Moore-Penrose residual check fails at atol=1e-15, while on the fixed revision (driver='ev', SYEV) it passes. Dependency versions are unconstrained in the evidence, so the strategy picks a modern numpy/scipy build from source at the buggy commit.

system_packages: libopenblas-dev or reference LAPACK (default scipy build backend)
pinned_because: numpy and scipy versions are null in documented constraints; the 1.18.1/1.4.1 versions in issue #12515 are reported in a version block, not a constraint, so they are not pinned and a buildable modern pair is chosen instead
LAPACK backend is the one scipy builds against; the SYEVR behaviour is driven by the LAPACK library, so the backend must be recorded when reproducing

strategy.reproducing_test: test_zero_eigenvalue in PinvhTests: a = [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]]; p = pinvh(a); assert_allclose(p @ a @ p, p, atol=1e-15); assert_allclose(a @ p @ a, a, atol=1e-15)
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision 237b6915e37e: test_zero_eigenvalue FAILS, because pinvh with the default evr driver keeps a spurious eigenvalue near 1e-17 (or 2.7e-15 per the evr report) above the cutoff, so p@a@p differs from p by more than atol=1e-15. Fixed revision (driver='ev'): test_zero_eigenvalue PASSES, because the SYEV driver yields a zero eigenvalue below the cutoff and the pseudoinverse satisfies the conditions to within atol.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np; from scipy.linalg import pinvh, eigh; a=np.array([[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]]); print(eigh(a,driver='evr',eigvals_only=True)); print(eigh(a,driver='ev',eigvals_only=True))"

input_output_examples.buggy_output: np.allclose(np.matmul(np.matmul(y1, x), y1), y1) returns False
input_output_examples.expected_output: np.allclose(np.matmul(np.matmul(y1, x), y1), y1) returns True (y1 should match pinv(x))

input_output_examples.input: sp.linalg.eigh(a, driver='evr') on the same matrix

risks: The defect is LAPACK-dependent: SYEVR's zero-eigenvalue error appears only with certain LAPACK builds (reference LAPACK vs OpenBLAS) and may not reproduce on a different backend, so the transition may not occur on every machine.
Dtype is not stated; the example uses integer literals which pinvh converts to float64, but a float32 run would have a different epsilon and could change the outcome.

The atol=1e-15 threshold is the developer's choice; the evidence does not state the separation point between correct and incorrect answers beyond that, so a different LAPACK may give residuals just below or above it.
Reproduction rate is not stated in the passages; the test may pass on the buggy revision on some machines, so a passing buggy run does not disprove the bug.
The fix is not to be backported, so running the test on other branches gives different results; use the exact commit pair only.
Dependency versions 1.18.1/1.4.1 are from the issue report and are not a documented constraint; building against modern numpy/scipy may not reproduce the era-specific LAPACK behaviour.

oracle.tolerance: atol=1e-15 on the Moore-Penrose residuals in test_zero_eigenvalue
oracle.reference_source: analytic eigenvalues 3, 1, 0 of the example matrix; pinv comparison in the issue
oracle.why: The residual check is the developer's own oracle; the zero eigenvalue is epsilon-scale so an absolute tolerance is required.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision pinvh uses the default evr driver, which returns a zero eigenvalue of about 3.9e-17 (or 2.7e-15) that the cutoff does not discard; the pseudoinverse then has a large component along that direction, so p@a@p differs from p by more than atol=1e-15 and assert_allclose raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision pinvh uses driver='ev' (SYEV), which gives the zero eigenvalue below the cutoff, so the pseudoinverse satisfies both Moore-Penrose residuals within atol=1e-15 and the test passes.
